      Fiscal Year 2026
      Capital Budget


Eric D. Batista, City Manager
Fiscal 2026 CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PLAN
______________________________________________________________________________

Budget Message

This comprehensive, five-year Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) for Fiscal Years 2026-2030 takes into account
the collective priorities of our community, City Council, and my administration following the vision of The
City of Worcester Strategic Plan: FY2025-2029. As we continue to implement a long-term strategy, we also
consider the need for flexibility during a time of increased capital borrowing costs.

Many of the capital projects proposed in this Capital Improvement Plan will have a positive impact during
Fiscal 2026, whereas some are multi-year programs that will yield results in the coming years. In the table
below, projects with prior year loan authorization depict ongoing facility and infrastructure programs for which
City Council has previously approved loan orders. Projects with new authorization in Fiscal 2026 represent
new projects and/or ongoing projects that require increased loan authority.

                        Remaining Prior Year    FY26 New                       Other Funding
  Funding Source                                              FY26 Borrowing
                           Authorization      Authorization                     (Grants, etc.)
Tax Levy                $        33,095,500 $     68,743,412 $      42,953,548 $   24,630,000
South Division                    1,500,000       47,000,000        11,000,000                 -
Golf Enterprise                     825,000        1,575,000           100,000                 -
Off Street Parking                2,610,000          300,000         1,415,000      2,000,000

DCU                               7,000,000                 -        2,240,000                 -
WPS - MSBA                       28,000,000                 -        9,400,000                 -
    Grand Total         $       100,230,500 $    158,938,412 $     113,099,548 $   32,080,000


In total, this Fiscal 2026 CIP recommends a total annual borrowing of $113M, $9.4M or 8% of which is related
to Worcester Public Schools – Massachusetts School Building Authority (MSBA) projects. The Fiscal 2026
CIP also includes a total tax levy capital borrowing of $42.95M, approximately $1.2M above Fiscal 2025
recommendations; enterprise and self-funded borrowing of $49.7M, and $32M in potential grant funding to
be invested in the City. I am recommending $158.9M in new loan authorization for Fiscal 2026 to be approved
by City Council. These recommendations include mission critical equipment like new public safety vehicles
in Police, and Fire; investments in wireless expansion in City parks; investments in core assets like our public
schools, police headquarters, and fire stations, including the construction of a new South Division Fire Station;
the design of safer, more inclusive streets through the Department of Transportation and Mobility, as well as
the maintenance of our streets and sidewalks through the Department of Public Works; and finally, the
beautification of our city through the efforts of the restructured Parks Department. Additionally, we are
recommending key investments in our Water, Sewer, Golf, and Off-Street Parking enterprise accounts.

Equipment

For Fiscal 2026, I am recommending a total investment of $9.3M in new equipment borrowing, of which
$4.7M is tax levy supported. Notable purchases include a $1.8M investment into the public works fleet,
$650K in Marked Police cruisers, and a $1M investment into the Parks fleet.

Other major equipment purchases include:

   •   $160K in Fire Prevention vehicles
   •   $500K in Public Schools related equipment
   •   $360K in various security camera installations and replacements
   •   $250K in Wi-Fi expansion at various parks
   •   $4.4M total between Water and Sewer equipment

Facility Improvement

I am recommending an investment of $41.3M in facility improvements, $33.2M of which is tax levy
supported. The major contributor to this category is the beginning of construction of a new South Division
Fire Station totaling $11M in anticipated Fiscal 2026 borrowing.

Other facility improvement projects include:

   •   $9.4M in MSBA related projects at Doherty High School and Burncoat High School and Middle School
   •   $3.5M for non-MSBA school rehabilitation
   •   $2.1M for WPD headquarters generator, HVAC and plumbing work
   •   $300K for rehabilitation projects at the City’s various fire stations
   •   $2.2M for DCU renovations
   •   $1.8M for Union Station as a match to Federal Transit Authority grant funding
   •   $1M for DPW building projects
   •   $1M for continued work on the roof of the Worcester Memorial Auditorium
   •   $4.6M for Water to fund pump station and filtration plant related work



                                                                                                              2
Fiscal 2026 CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PLAN
______________________________________________________________________________
Infrastructure

Of the $94.6M recommended in infrastructure upgrades, we recommend $10.6M in borrowing for
resurfacing and other street and sidewalk related construction projects to be allocated to the Department
of Public Works, $3.3M be allocated to the Department of Transportation and Mobility for street design and
traffic signals, and $8.2M to Parks for various parks related improvements.


Other infrastructure projects include:

   •   $20.8M for various sewer infrastructure projects including interceptor rehabilitation and
       reconstruction projects, as well as sewage flow analysis to ensure the city’s ability to grow
       sustainably.
   •   $2M for the redesign and construction of streets in the Green Island neighborhood, in conjunction
       with associated Community Development Block Grant funding, to address drainage issues in the
       area.
   •   $7.82M for various water projects including improvements to water mains, as well as repairs and
       replacement of water meters
   •   $6M for water main construction related to the grant funded redesign of Chandler Street.

WPS Equipment and Facility Improvement

I am recommending a total of $5M for various equipment purchases and facility repairs for the Worcester
Public Schools. This includes $4.5M for general building rehabilitation, $1M of which will come from
Community Development Block Grant funds and the remainder from Tax Levy, and $500K in capital
equipment funding. In addition, as referenced above, I am recommending approximately $9.4M, including
State contributions, for Massachusetts School Building Authority-related projects, primarily to complete the
construction of the new Doherty Memorial High School, and begin a feasibility study of a replacement
Burncoat High School and Middle School.

Budget Process

Putting fiscal responsibility first and foremost, the Budget Office developed an analytical budget process
ensuring all capital requests are assessed and prioritized to formulate a sound, long-term Capital
Improvement Plan. As we evaluate the City’s short- and long-term capital needs, our current resources and
expectations, and the potential of grant funds, we believe the current proposed Fiscal 2026 Capital
Improvement Plan represents a solid investment in the City and will assist in maintaining our capacity to
respond to present conditions while setting a foundation for continued growth and expansion.

Capital & Debt Policy

   •   The City will maintain a multi-year approach for the Capital Improvement Plan
   •   A capital asset is defined as an asset that has a useful life of one year or more
   •   Any capital asset to be financed shall have a minimal unit cost of $5,000, and a useful life of five
       years or more
   •   Capital assets with a unit cost of less than $5,000 and/or a useful life of less than 5 years are to be
       purchased with cash through the Operating Budget under the Capital Outlay accounts

                                                                                                                 3
Fiscal 2026 CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PLAN
______________________________________________________________________________
   •   The City will obtain financing only when necessary
   •   Debt financing will not be considered appropriate for recurring costs such as operating and
       maintenance expenditures
   •   The City will utilize external bond counsel for all debt issuances
   •   Continual review of all outstanding debts will be undertaken to determine refunding opportunities
   •   The City will seek to amortize general obligation bonds with level principal and interest costs over
       the life of the issue
   •   The City will seek to issue its general bond obligations in a competitive sale unless determined that
       such a sale method will not produce the best results for the City.

Traffic & Signal Engineering - Design and implementation of traffic signal and related intersection improvements, including a new signal at the Massasoit and Sunderland Rd. intersection.

Temporary Speed Humps - Purchase and installation of temporary speed humps in various locations throughout the City.

Security Camera Installation - Security camera upgrades and installations at various parks.
Aquatics - Upgrades to include painting, UV system upgrades, equipment replacement, and surface replacement of the East Park Spray Park.
Bell Pond - Funding for renovations to the beach, building, parking lot, and basketball court.
Bennett Field - Department of Environmental Protection required contaminated soil removal.
Dog Parks - Purchases of obstacles, and surface replacement.
Great Brook Valley Park - Softball field construction, walkway accessibility, construction of an information booth, climate resiliency improvements, parking lot upgrades, and other general improvements.
Holmes Field - CSX funding for the installation of lighting in and around the playground.
Hope Cemetery - Redesign of the maintenance barn.
Lincoln Square Memorial - Continued monument work associated with the senior housing development.
Playground Renovations - Replacement of playground safety surfacing, and other general playground related upgrades.
South Worcester Playground - Construction a new basketball court, handball court, installation of lighting, new fencing, accessible walkways, updated security infrastructure, as well as other general improvements.
Worcester Common - Sidewalk reconstruction around the Common, to begin along Franklin Street.
Auditorium - Continued design and construction for the roof of the Worcester Memorial Auditorium.
Parks Capital Equip - Various equipment and vehicle purchases essential to Parks, Forestry and Cemetery Services' operations.
Parks Building Upgrades - General building upgrades at various parks.
Tacoma Street Park - Completion of soil remediation and construction at Tacoma Street Park.
East Park Building - Construction of a new support building at the newly renovated little league field.
Lakeview Park - Replacement of the playground and basketball court, additional benches, picnic tables, and lighting, tree planting, and other general improvements.
